hook.text: By 2000, JavaScript was considered a 'toy language' by serious programmers.

buildup.text: It was used for annoying pop-ups, blinking text, and broken form validation.

discovery.text: Users disabled JavaScript entirely. Many sites worked better without it.

twist.text: The language itself wasn't bad — the uses were. Developers hadn't learned its strengths yet.

climax.text: JavaScript's redemption arc from toy language to dominant platform was just beginning.

punchline.text: The most hated language became the most used.

quiz.question: Why did many users disable JavaScript around 2000?
